note: Expected seconds of `wstest` time per case, per group. `planShards` multiplies this by the group's measured case count, so correcting either re-prices the split. Both columns are measurements, not derivations: the counts are the realised per-group case totals from run 36287763043, and the per-case cost is what that run's wall clock divided by its case count implies.
provenance: Measured in autobahn.yml run 36287763043 on ubuntu-24.04, which ran the 301-case framing selection as four concurrent shards and finished the suite step in 14s. That is the first run in which the engine passed almost everything, and it changed the cost model completely. The suite used to take 2100s, and the difference is not per-case work: the report's own per-case `duration` sums to 12s across all 301 cases, because `duration` spans `caseStart` at `onOpen` to `caseEnd` at `connectionLost` and so excludes the TCP connect and the opening handshake the client does per case. What the old 2100s actually was is failing cases waiting on the client's close-handshake timeout, and 229 of them were failing. Fixing the engine removed the timeouts and with them the cost, which is why sharding's contribution is now small next to it.
units: seconds of suite step time per case
